page: UpCloud PREMIUM-4xCPU-16GB is a general purpose cloud server configured with 4 shared vCPUs and 16.0 GB of memory on KVM virtualization. Powered by AMD EPYC 9575F processors built on the x86_64 architecture running at 2.0 GHz, each vCPU maps to a dedicated physical core with one thread per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, 16 MB of L3 cache, and instruction support for AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16, alongside AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic operations. The instance bundles 150 GB of local SSD storage and includes one public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core compute performance alongside standard multi-core throughput. The server scores in the top 10 percent for stress-ng single-core execution and Geekbench single-core testing, reaching 2,251 points. Single-threaded data handling reflects similar strength, achieving top-decile throughput in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. In contrast, overall multi-core throughput aligns with the median tier, registering a Geekbench multi-core score of 6,352 and 14,889.36 in stress-ng. Synthetic memory evaluation reveals lower relative throughput, with PassMark memory testing falling into the bottom quartile despite uncached memory read bandwidth measuring 113.71 GB/s and write bandwidth measuring 55.21 GB/s.

The hardware configuration provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, optimizing resource density for standard production services. Because the shared CPU allocation is coupled with high per-core single-threaded speed and local SSD storage, it delivers dependable execution efficiency without dedicated compute tier costs. Workload fit includes web application serving, mid-sized database management, CI/CD runners, and text processing tasks that benefit from fast single-threaded performance rather than deep parallel scaling.
